# jenkins_credential_vault_ssh (Resource)

Manages a Vault SSH username with private key credential within Jenkins. The username, private key, and passphrase are resolved from Vault at runtime, so no secret material is stored within Jenkins or in Terraform state.

~> The Jenkins installation that uses this resource is expected to have the [Hashicorp Vault Plugin](https://plugins.jenkins.io/hashicorp-vault-plugin/) installed in their system.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "jenkins_credential_vault_ssh" "example" {
  name = "example-vault-ssh"
  path = "secret/data/example/ssh"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name of the resource being created. This maps to the ID property within Jenkins, and cannot be changed once set.
- `path` (String) The Vault path of the secret to read.

### Optional

- `description` (String) A human readable description of the credentials being stored.
- `domain` (String) The domain store to place the credentials into. If not set will default to the global credentials store.
- `engine_version` (Number) The KV engine version of the Vault secrets engine. Must be either `1` or `2`. Defaults to `2`, which pins the credential rather than inheriting the Jenkins global or folder Vault configuration.
- `folder` (String) The folder namespace to store the resource in. If not set will default to global Jenkins.
- `namespace` (String) The Vault namespace to read the secret from.
- `passphrase_key` (String) The key within the Vault secret to read the private key passphrase from. Defaults to `passphrase`.
- `prefix_path` (String) The Vault mount prefix path to prepend to `path`.
- `private_key_key` (String) The key within the Vault secret to read the private key from. Defaults to `private_key`.
- `scope` (String) The visibility of the credentials to Jenkins agents. This must be set to either "GLOBAL" or "SYSTEM". If not set will default to "GLOBAL".
- `username_key` (String) The key within the Vault secret to read the username from. Defaults to `username`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The full canonical job path, e.g. `/job/job-name`
